sections.heading: The bank inside the tower
sections.body:
Albert Pissis's Anglo and London Paris National Bank of 1910 stands within the tower, its granite front carrying 38-foot Doric columns; its banking hall is the atrium the public open space occupies. The bronze Star Maiden in it is a 1985 cast of a figure Alexander Stirling Calder made for the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition, commissioned with the permission of the sculptor's daughter Margaret Calder Hayes.
Sources disagree about the bank's date: Wikipedia gives 1910, SPUR's guide 1912.

historic_survey.note: Citigroup Center by William Pereira & Associates, whose greenhouse atrium privately owned public open space sits inside the shell of a former bank of about 1910 by Albert Pissis - an early case of a POPOS built around a retained piece of the older city.

historical_record.description: The Holbrook Building stood here from 1912 until the tower replaced it — seven storeys over a basement around a central lightwell, a steel skeleton with reinforced concrete walls and floors, composed as a three-part vertical block to the design of MacDonald and Applegarth.
The Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board recommended city landmark status and the Planning Commission agreed on 4 January 1979, but the Board of Supervisors refused the designation on 2 April 1979.

City landmark status for the Anglo and London Paris National Bank building was recommended by the Landmarks Preservation Advisory Board and by the Planning Commission on 4 January 1979, and refused by the Board of Supervisors on 2 April 1979.
The Citicorp project going up on this corner kept a part of the exterior walls of the Anglo-California Bank building, reused as an entrance court for the office tower.
One Sansome Street, designed by architect William Pereira.
